title: The algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q$ inside $\Qlb$
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$ for the field of $\ell$-adic numbers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and use
the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber].
The field $\Qlb$ has characteristic $0$ and is an extension of $\mathbf Q$ through its prime subfield [def-pc-field-extension]. Set

$$
\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}=
\{z\in\Qlb:z\text{ is algebraic over }\mathbf Q\},
$$

the algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q$ in $\Qlb$ [def-weil-algebraic-element, def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure]: a subfield of $\Qlb$ containing $\mathbf Q$. (That it is algebraically closed, hence an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q$, and that the realizations below exist, is the statement lem-weil-realization-exists, which is proved from this definition and is not part of it.) Fix an algebraic
closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. A $\mathbf Q$-isomorphism (a bijective $\mathbf Q$-embedding)
$\jmath:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim} \overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}$ [def-weil-field-extension-isomorphism] is an *$\ell$-adic realization of algebraic
numbers*.

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against the master blueprint (sk-thm-intfactors/def-weil-algebraic-closure-q.md; no slopmaster2 copy; Lean state none). Kept the objects but made every notion a statement dependency: Q_ℓ (def-weil-l-adic-numbers), algebraic closures of Q_ℓ and of Q (def-weil-algebraic-closure), the Q-structure of a characteristic-0 field (def-pc-field-extension), and three new Mathlib-leaf definitions: def-weil-algebraic-element (IsAlgebraic), def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure (algebraicClosure F E, giving that Q̄^(ℓ) is a subfield), def-weil-field-extension-isomorphism (AlgEquiv/AlgHom). The blueprint's sentence 'This is an algebraically closed subfield' is a claim, not data: the subfield part is the Mathlib definition, and 'algebraically closed' plus the existence of a realization are lem-weil-realization-exists, which depends on this node, so it is named in the text but cannot be a dependency (it would close a cycle). 'Q-embedding ȷ: Q̄ ≅ Q̄^(ℓ)' was made precise as a Q-isomorphism, as lem-weil-realization-exists reads it. def-weil-finite-field-fiber is kept since the statement uses the datum (only for ℓ ≠ p; the notion itself does not depend on p). In Lean the whole definition is `Qbar ≃ₐ[ℚ] algebraicClosure ℚ (AlgebraicClosure ℚ_[ℓ])`, so every branch below ends in Mathlib leaves except def-weil-finite-field-fiber.
